# CS-34 — Team working agreement

!!! info "Case card"
    **Difficulty:** Intermediate (CS-21..CS-45) ·
    **Level:** L1 — Single-concept drill ·
    **Domain:** D9 · **Seed project:** standalone

## Learning objectives

1. Convert recurring dysfunctions into behavioral norms.
2. Design light-touch enforcement that survives disagreement.

## Project context

A capstone team's retros keep surfacing the same three issues: silent disagreement in meetings followed by Monday-morning objections; one member carrying integration work every sprint; meetings running 20 minutes over with no decisions.

## Problem statement

Write a working agreement whose items directly counter those three dysfunctions.

## Constraints and available information

- 6–8 items; each item must map to one of the three dysfunctions.
- Each item: behavior, not aspiration ('we trust each other' is banned).
- Include the enforcement mechanism for one violated item.

## Student tasks

1. Draft the agreement with dysfunction mapping.
2. Write the enforcement protocol for one item.
3. Define the review cadence for the agreement itself.

## Expected deliverables

- Working agreement card with mapping.
- Enforcement protocol.

## Discussion questions

1. Why do working agreements decay, and what slows the decay?
1. Is an agreement signed with the instructor present more or less durable?

## How you will be graded

Items are behavioral and mapped (50%); enforcement is concrete and proportionate (30%); review cadence defined (20%).

## Where this case appears

- Anchored in [Lecture 25](../lectures/L25-25-team-performance.md).
- Suggested use: in-class.
